claims.text: The alloy system is (W1.5Ni2.25Fe)95Ta5 at.% and has a dual-phase BCC/FCC structure.
The as-cast alloy has a yield strength of approximately 600 MPa.
The initial alloy is brittle because of a coarse microstructure or the absence of coherent precipitates.
The processing route comprises hot rolling at 1200 °C with 80% reduction, cold rolling at 25 °C with 75% reduction, annealing at 900 °C for 5 min, aging at 650 °C for 20 h, and water quenching.
Room-temperature tensile testing is performed at a strain rate of 5 × 10^-4 s^-1, with additional testing up to 800 °C and characterization by EBSD, TEM, STEM, and APT.
The stepwise route produces multiple coherent precipitation structures consisting of δ lamellae and γ″ particles.
The δ lamellae are approximately 40 nm wide and the spheroidal γ″ particles are approximately 10 nm in size.
The δ lamellae have a D0a structure and the γ″ particles have a D022 structure.
Coherent interfaces permit dislocations to shear the δ lamellae, thereby relieving stress concentrations.
The γ″ particles pin dislocations through order hardening.
The combined δ-lamella shearing and γ″-particle pinning mechanisms produce a synergistic strength–ductility improvement.
After δ-lamella precipitation the yield strength reaches approximately 1.4 GPa, and after γ″-particle precipitation it reaches approximately 2.0 GPa.
The precipitation architecture maintains high strain-hardening rates and prevents premature crack initiation.
The processed alloy achieves an ultimate tensile strength of approximately 2.15 GPa and tensile ductility of approximately 15% at room temperature.
The stepwise process simultaneously enhances strength and ductility and thereby avoids the conventional strength–ductility trade-off.
Conventional single-step aging or long-duration annealing produces coarse or incoherent precipitates or grain growth, yielding either strength or ductility but not both.
The stepwise route significantly outperforms standard thermal treatments.
The proposed mechanism requires coherent D0a and D022 ordered precipitates in a dual-phase BCC/FCC refractory alloy.
The mechanism may fail when the precipitates are incoherent or when the matrix lacks the necessary stacking-fault energy.
